title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, was arrested at gunpoint at her Tennessee home in July 2025 while babysitting four children. Fargo police used AI facial recognition to match her social media photo to a fake ID used by a bank fraud suspect. She spent nearly four months in a Tennessee jail without bail, then about two more months in North Dakota. Charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time. She was released on Christmas Eve and later learned she had lost her home and car.

Lipps is suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10m in federal court. The lawsuit says the detective relied on facial recognition without enough investigation or probable cause, and that the police department lacked proper policies, training, and supervision for the technology. It also says she was denied medications and dentures in jail and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The suit seeks damages and accountability, and Lipps hopes it will make officers more careful when using AI facial recognition.
